voice.script: For students, freshers and those starting their careers, a degree is a foundation. In an AI-shaped world, workplace readiness takes more. Ascend helps you discover suitable roles, identify skill gaps and practise realistic industry tasks. Its AI gives constructive feedback to improve each attempt. Prepare for interviews and build a professional identity backed by your work. Ascend helps you become job-ready and stand out in a crowded field of job seekers. Colleges can focus their support. For employers facing thousands of applications, Ascend brings work artifacts, skill evidence and interview readiness into view. Its proposed Productivity Index connects role-specific readiness with supporting evidence, showing demonstrated capabilities and gaps still to develop. The aim: clearer hiring decisions, with less time and cost to productivity. Ascend. A talent fulfilment network, bridging the productivity gap.

film.note: Beat voice boundaries are editorial targets; align cuts after measuring the recorded narration. Use natural pauses and rewrite if needed. Do not time-stretch speech or duplicate footage to fill time.

welcome.style: Three distinct real human workplace moments. One meaningful action each, subtle background activity and a short forward dolly. Play once, hold, replay control. Never orbit or loop endlessly.
welcome.changes: Use six seconds rather than four because this model's supported six-second 1080p request is quoted at the same 10 credits as the earlier four-second 720p option.

continuity: Reuse character identities, outfits, physical objects, daylight and color palette; not the actual clips, framings or primary actions. No human mentor. App feedback is the guidance. Employer office and props are unbranded; Ascend appears on screens only.
qualityGate: Natural faces, hands, eyes and object contact throughout, not just attractive first frame.
Purposeful gestures and subtle background life; no frozen pan-only output or excessive acting.
Stable screen plane suitable for actual UI replacement, no morphing generated interface text.

No reused full-screen welcome footage in the 60-second film.
